Subject Name Automation hub: BNL - SAL/LOG/MKT - Send SPE to Order Requests & Process Feedback
Purpose:
Joint request from the BNL local Demand & Supply & Marketing departments.

The purpose of these workflows is to simplify the 'SPE to Order' process. The local Marketing non-catalogue team (Products & Services) & the local non-catalogue demand planner (Demand & Supply) collaborate in a 'SPE to Order' work file in which all new replenishment requests for customer specific articles get logged and tracked. 

In the 'as is' situation, each of these requests need to get sent manually to the responsible commercial colleagues, which amounts to hundreds of e-mails that need to be sent on a monthly basis, which in its turn generates additional traffic, overhead and time spent on back and forth over something that should be a simple request.

In order to automate, simplify and standardize this process three separate workflows have been developed.
The BNL LOG/MKT Extract SPE to Order PBI workflow that was developed previously will serve as the source data for these two other scripts.

The second UiPath workflow (BNL LOG Send SPE to Order Requests to SAL) is a script that will be launched on a bi-weekly basis, every Tuesday and Thursday at 3:00 AM CET. 
This script is used to automatically send the customer specific replenishment requests to the responsible commercial colleagues. The work file tracks which requests have been sent to which account managers on which date. Every new row in the file without sales feedback results in a new request getting sent to the responsible AM, containing their unique request ID. If a previously processed row has not received any feedback after two weeks, the responsible AM will receive a reminder.

The third workflow (BNL SAL Process SPE to Order Feedback) is reactive in nature and will be launched every time the designated 'SPE To Order' MS Form gets completed by a sales colleague. This will trigger a PA Cloud workflow which in its turn will launch a UiPath workflow using an API trigger. This workflow will connect to the Excel Online version of the work file and process the sales feedback and any other additional comments in the row that contains the unique request ID. If by accident a Form was filled in that does not correspond to any row in the work file, the responder will receive an alert prompting them to verify and try again.

Purpose:

Background:Transaction ZW55 in SAP is used to transfer updates from customer cards and chain structures in SAP to NetShop. Since February 12, 2025, this transfer occurs automatically every 30 minutes, based on change pointers on the customer card. The information is sent as an IDoc and automatically read into NetShop via a cus-file. (Exact time when Admin clears its log is unknown)
Before the automatic run was introduced, transaction ZW55 had to be run manually to send changes. This means that there are historical changes today that have not yet been transferred to NetShop.
Purpose:We now need to manually trigger the transfer of our entire customer register – including customer numbers and invoice recipients – to ensure that NetShop has the latest information.
Challenge:It is not possible to trigger the entire register in one run because NetShop has a limitation on how many customer numbers can be handled per read-in. Historically, we have not run more than 1,000 customer numbers at a time to avoid the cus-file becoming too large and difficult to read into Admin.
Number to be mass-run:Customer numbers: approx. 240k Invoice recipients: approx. 100k
Planned working method (robot):
Start from a total file in Excel with customer numbers in one column.
Divide the list into blocks of approximately 1,000 customer numbers at a time.
Enter SAP transaction ZW55, input the customer numbers, and save.
After about 15 minutes, go into Admin and manually read in the generated cus-file.
Repeat the process every 15–30 minutes until the entire register is updated.

Subject Name Automation hub: BNL - MKT - Pricing ZM003008 Mass Re-Upload
Purpose:
Request from the local Products & Services (Marketing Department)

During the end of year pricing update process the local Products & Services (Marketing) department in Benelux needs to upload all new purchase prices in SAP. In order to do this they need to extract a file on a per supplier basis from the SAP transaction ZM003007. Afterwards, this supplier file gets matched with a purchase price bible that contains the new price for the coming year, as well as the corresponding unit. 

These two parts of the process have already been automated previously, you can find the respective projects under the following Automation Hub card titles:
BNL - MKT - Pricing ZM003007 Mass Download 
BNL - MKT - Pricing Purchase Price Match
There is however one more part that had been done manually until now, which is re-uploading all these supplier files in SAP, more specifically in transaction ZM003008.
Doing this manually generates a significant workload for multiple employees. Given the repetitive nature of the actions that need to be carried out per iteration, a request was made to also automate this part of the process using RPA.

The UiPath workflow will fetch all 'To upload' files in a specific SharePoint folder and iterate through them. For each file in the designated folder, the script will check whether it concerns a core 'CAT' product file, or a non-core 'SPX' product file, given that these types of products need to be re-uploaded with a different 'Valid To' date in the designates SAP transaction. The script will upload the file using pre-set parameters (Valid From / Valid To / Percent Rate) and keep track of a possible pop-up message that states whether the file contains products price changes outside of the pre-set boundaries or not. Exceptions will get logged, as well as files that got skipped due to being unresolvable in terms of 'Type of file'.

The script will be triggered periodically, but this should be limited to a few times per year given that these uploads will only be required during a specific part of the End of Year Pricing process (and possibly the Mid Year Pricing process).

Subject Name Automation hub: BNL - FIN - CM Customer Aging - Daily Report
Purpose:
Request from the local Credit manager, Finance Department.

Periodical reports concerning the aging of customers are made using a lot of data extracted from SAP. Part of this data comes from the 'ZFDOPR10 - Customer Open Item Analysis (Overdue Items Balance)' transaction. Local variants have been made in SAP that group data from multiple data tables in a display that is generated in the transaction.

An upside to its FBL5N counterpart is that there is an option to request the data in a background/spool process, so this request does not have to run completely on the foreground. Depending on the company code and the amount of items requested this background process can take a long time. Requesting this data for all the company codes in the Benelux organisation requires the user to wait more than an hour.
In order to be able to free up a significant amount of time a request was made to automate this process.

Two separate UiPath workflows have been created for this process. 
The first workflow will iterate through the different company codes of Lyreco Benelux in SAP transaction ZFDOPR10 and request a report per company code on a virtual machine outside of office hours, so that no users nor physical machines are hindered during the runtime of the request. 
The second workflow will fetch the daily results per company code in SAP transaction SM37 and export them to an .XLSX file which is subsequently cleaned to improve readability. The processed file per company code will be uploaded to a SharePoint location and shared with the process owners.

The script will be triggered on a daily basis.

Subject Name Automation hub: BNL - FIN - Distance Calculation - Update Employee Details
Purpose:
Request from the local Payroll manager, Finance Department.

On a monthly basis the local payroll department extracts a report from ProTime (local platform) containing all declared travel expenses. The report contains a list of entries made by Benelux colleagues in the platform, containing details such as their default workplace and the place of the 'activity'.
The remuneration of this declaration is based on the travel distance in kilometres. In order to calculate the remuneration the local payroll team would have to manually calculate the distance using tools such as Google Maps / Bing Maps. 
Given the repetitive nature of this activity and the possibility of 1000+ entries being in the monthly files, a request was made to automate/optimize this process.

A previous development was made in the Power Automate platform, which would iterate through the list of entries and would calculate the difference between 'Point A' and 'Point B' using a Bing Maps API connection. The calculation is however based on the personal addresses of the employees, but this data is not available in the ProTime platform. These details need to get fetched from WorkDay exports.

This process (UiPath cloud workflow / background process) will feed a local database with the report details so that the PA cloud process making the actual calculations can use up to date data. 
The script will be triggered on a monthly basis based on the schedule of the WorkDay exports.

Subject Name Automation hub: BNL - MKT - Pricing Purchase Price Match
Purpose:
Request from the local Products & Services (Marketing Department)

During the end of year pricing update process the local Products & Services (Marketing) department in Benelux needs to upload all the new purchase prices in SAP. The new purchase prices are stored in a local 'Purchase Price Bible', which contains roughly 25K lines. The new purchase prices need to be filled in in a 'per supplier' file. Each supplier has 2 separate files, one for all 'Core' products and one for the 'Non-core' products. This amounts to roughly 800 files that need to be completed.
Doing this manually generates a significant workload for multiple employees. Previously this would be done by using V-Lookup / X-Lookup formulas in Excel. This would amount to multiple full working days being spent on this task by multiple employees of each separate product category. Given the repetitive nature of the actions that need to be carried out per iteration, a request was made to automate this process using RPA.

The UiPath workflow will read an Excel file and store all unique references and their corresponding new purchase price. These lines will be stored in a virtual data table. The script will subsequently read every separate 'per supplier' .CSV file and match all lines in them with the references in the virtual data table. If a match is found, the new purchase price will be written back to the 'per supplier' file. The workflow will log how many files have been processed and it will also verify whether there were any files that didn't have a single matching line in the source data table.
Each file that is processed will be uploaded to a specific SharePoint folder using the Office 365 Integration Service activities, so that all files are saved on a location that is accessible by the local Products & Services colleagues.

The script will be triggered periodically, but this should be limited to a few times per year given that these files will only be required during a specific part of the End of Year Pricing process (and possibly the Mid Year Pricing process).

Subject Name Automation hub: SWE - CS - Invoice changes - Credit / debit
Purpose:
The objective is to fully automate all processes within SAP whenever we need to modify or manipulate an invoice.
The central aspect of this automation involves initiating a credit process for the existing invoice and subsequently initiating a debit process to generate a corrected version:
There are multiple variations that utilize the same core approach (credit and debit). Examples include changing invoice addresses or references, correcting article prices, handling goodwill compensations, and more.
Version 1 is ready for debugging in the production environment as soon as it becomes unattended. Our intention is to continuously expand support for different versions to address a wide range of scenarios.
The goal is to replace the practice of raising a support ticket with our backoffice unit operations support. Instead, we will utilize the UiPath application to trigger the necessary steps within SAP.
We anticipate approximately 1 full-time equivalent (FTE) in savings, as well as a substantial reduction in lead time for these types of errors (currently taking around 2-4 days under normal circumstances, and more when the backlog is extensive). This improvement will result in an enhanced customer experience and a decrease in incoming calls.

Request from the local Products & Services (Marketing) department in Benelux.

For the end of year pricing requests will be sent out en masse to our suppliers in order to receive the pricing for their product assortment of the coming year.
A different UiPath workflow (BNL MKT Pricing Data Split) will split up the source data in a separate file on a 'per supplier basis'. Each file per supplier will be sent out automatically using a series of Power Automate cloud flows.
In the weeks following the mass mailing the suppliers will be sending their completed pricelists back to the local marketing colleagues. These files will be validated and forwarded to a different box which has a reactive Power Automate cloud flow on it which will automatically save the files on a specific Sharepoint site in a specific subfolder.

This request entails the consolidation of data that has been sent by the suppliers. A large amount of files are received by the local marketing department, and consolidating them manually would cost a lot of time and could also be prone to errors/inaccuracies. Rather than doing this manually, a request was made for an RPA solution that would cover this need automatically.
The UiPath workflow will read all Excel files that have been received in the specified SharePoint folder and store all the lines in a virtual data table if the file is valid. In case of an invalid file structure the workflow skips the file. Subsequently, the full data table will be appended to the consolidated file. Doing this, the consolidated file will always contain all the received information without users having to complete it manually. Processed files will be saved in a separate folder and the processing date will also be noted on a line level basis in the main file. Doing this, it will be easy to check which lines correspond to which file per supplier.

The process is ready for unattended use on a VM using the O365 connector and package. The process runs once per day using a scheduled trigger in the UiPath Orchestrator environment. At the end of the workflow the results will get sent to the process owners including the amount of files processed and/or skipped during the daily run.

Subject Name Automation hub: BNL - Supply - Release of Blocked invoice lines w/ Quantity discrepancies
Purpose:
On a periodic basis our local Demand & Supply team extracts a report from SAP containing a list of invoice lines which are currently blocked for payment in our SAP environment due to a discrepancy between the quantity on the invoice and the quantity of said purchase order line in our SAP environment.

These lines need to be checked and subsequently released in the SAP transaction 'MRBR' on a line level basis by a local Demand & Supply colleague if it is deemed "clear for release". Each separate line needs to be selected by specifying the correct SAP document number, the purchase order number, and the line number. The 'Quantity block' cell in the SAP table needs to be selected, the blocking reason needs to be released and the save button needs to be pressed. These actions need to be repeated for every single line that is marked "clear for release".

Due to the highly repetitive nature of these actions, this process presents an interesting opportunity for an automated solution. The current build of the 'Blocked Invoices Release MRBRQ' Workflow was created in UiPath Studio. The workflow will use the Excel file containing the lines marked "clear for release" as source and create a data table to be used in the subsequent steps. The line details will be keyed in the MRBR transaction and the line in question will be requested. If a match was found in SAP for the line details in the XLSX file, the line will be released. If for whatever reason a match was not found in the SAP environment, a warning message will get returned.

Each action well get repeated for every line that was marked "clear for release".
Lines that have been released will be logged in a separate tab of the file, leaving the unprocessed lines for further checks or the next batch.

Subject Name Automation hub: BNL - Supply - Supplier Invoicing - MIRO Actions
Purpose:
Our Demand & Supply Planning Team gets a large amount of invoices from suppliers on a daily basis.
On a yearly basis receive over 35.000 invoices from our suppliers. Usually these are sent as .PDF
attachments of an E-mail. The majority of these invoices are processed by colleagues from the
Demand & Supply Planning Team. In very exceptional cases, invoices are processed as .XML file
using an EDI connection. In all other cases the processing of the received invoice consists of a series
of manual actions.

Processing the received supplier invoices consists of a series of actions that are carried out in our SAP
environment. Excluding exceptional cases, a lot of these actions can be seen as repetitive and of little
added value. Regardless, these actions need to be carried out continuously and with great care given
the impact of this process. Given the repetitive nature of some of these actions, there is little added
value to gain from doing them manually. This creates a major opportunity for improvement through
standardization and the implementation of automation solutions.

The goal of this project is to standardize and automate the supplier invoicing process for as many suppliers as possible.
We try to achieve this using technology and software from different fields of discipline. Invoices that are received from suppliers in the scope of our project will get automatically forwarded to a specific folder that is being monitored by our OCR software Abbyy FlexiCapture Studio 12. New files automatically get examined by our OCR software and all the details important for the invoicing process are stored in an .XLS database. The extracted results are keyed in automatically using an RPA-enhanced process created in the UiPath Studio environment.
Manual treatment is only required for exceptions.

After all preliminary checks have been carried out, the remaining validated lines in the .XLSX file are
cleared for further processing in SAP. The actual keying in of the invoice details happens in the MIRO
transaction of our SAP environment. 

For each invoice that needs to be processed a data table will be generated from the details present in the
database. Once all lines from a specific invoice/purchase order have been generated in the previously
mentioned data table, the first actions in the SAP transaction are carried out.
First, the workflow fills in all invoice specific details. Before being able to move on to line specific details, the workflow might have to deal with a couple of pop-ups and other menus. 
For example: if the purchase order was a direct delivery, an extra context menu will pop up for this
specific purpose. The UiPath workflow needs to be capable to handle all sorts of possible exceptions that might be the case for the invoice it is currently processing.

An extensive exception handling has been added to the workflow in order to deal with all possible
exceptions we are currently aware of. This is subject to change as we expand the scope of the project.
We will keep on training the workflow to be able to handle all future exceptions as well.
